A MODERN DICTIONARY OF DREAMS
=============================

Traditional dream meanings rewritten in plain contemporary English from four
public-domain dream books (Project Gutenberg), with a modern reading of the
feelings involved and questions for reflection.

The "tone" runs from ●○○○○ (very negative omen) to ●●●●● (very positive omen).
The omens come from the old books: read them as cultural history, not
prediction.

At the end, an index sends synonyms to their entries (e.g. "loaf → see
BREAD").



——————————  A  ——————————


Dreaming of Abandonment
───────────────────────

In one sentence
A dream of abandonment is mostly about the future: plans that are hard to
build, or ties you fear losing.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative, with one happy exception

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are abandoned: you struggle to make plans for the future
• You abandon someone: troubles pile up around you
• You leave your house: a setback when you try your luck
• You leave your sweetheart: lost valuables stay lost and friends turn away
• You leave a lover: an unexpected inheritance, the one happy sign
• You abandon your children or your business: losses and quarrels through lack
  of calm
• An abandoned ship: a business failure, unless you make it to shore

Depending on how you felt
• Fear or sadness: the dream often reflects a worry about being left out
• Relief: it may express a wish to leave a burden or situation behind

Questions to ask yourself
• Is there a relationship or project I feel slipping away?
• Am I the one who wants to walk away from something?

Related dreams: Forsaking · Exile · Farewell · Separation · Desert

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of an Abbess
─────────────────────

In one sentence
An abbess in a dream is about authority: something you give in to reluctantly,
unless she is kind.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed: constraint or true friends

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see an abbess: unpleasant tasks, and giving in to authority after a
  failed rebellion
• A smiling, kindly abbess: true friends and pleasing prospects

Depending on how you felt
• Irritation or rebellion: the dream may reflect an authority that weighs on
  you
• Calm: it may express a need for gentle guidance

Questions to ask yourself
• What rule or authority am I struggling to accept right now?
• Whose kind advice would I welcome?

Related dreams: Nun · Convent · Abbey · Abbot · Cloister

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of an Abbey
────────────────────

In one sentence
An abbey in a dream concerns your hopes: in ruins, it points to plans left
unfinished.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative, with an unexpected escape

Depending on what happens in the dream
• An abbey in ruins: your hopes and schemes end up unfinished
• A priest bars your way into an abbey: you are saved from ruin because rivals
  mistake your trouble for success
• You enter an abbey: a risk of serious illness
• You talk with a priest inside an abbey: true friends criticize an
  indiscretion

Depending on how you felt
• Nostalgia: the dream may reflect regret over a plan left half-done
• A need to withdraw: it may express a wish to shelter from the world

Questions to ask yourself
• What plan have I let fall into ruin?
• Do I need a quiet place to find myself again?

Related dreams: Ruin · Church · Cloister · Convent · Priest

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of an Abbot
────────────────────

In one sentence
An abbot in a dream warns against flattery and hidden schemes.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative, with one happy exception

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are an abbot: plots are being laid for your downfall
• An abbot at prayer: smooth flattery leads you willingly astray
• You talk with an abbot: you may give in to flattery and damage your
  reputation
• You marry an abbot: you keep your good name despite poverty and temptation,
  the one happy sign

Depending on how you felt
• Suspicion: the dream may reflect doubts about someone's sincerity
• Guilt: it may express a fear of having given in too easily to praise

Questions to ask yourself
• Who is flattering me right now, and why?
• Am I being won over by pretty words?

Related dreams: Monk · Priest · Abbey · Clergyman · Hypocrite

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of the Abdomen
───────────────────────

In one sentence
The abdomen in a dream is about expectations, effort and worries over loved
ones' health.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative, with one hopeful outcome

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see your abdomen: great expectations, if you work harder and rein in
  pleasure
• A shriveled abdomen: false friends persecute you
• A swollen abdomen: hardships, but you will overcome them and enjoy what you
  have earned
• Blood oozing from the abdomen: an accident or tragedy in the family
• A child's sickly abdomen: a risk of contagion

Depending on how you felt
• Worry: the dream often reflects concern about your own or your family's
  health
• Vulnerability: it may express a fear of being hurt where you are weakest

Questions to ask yourself
• What am I struggling to digest right now?
• Am I taking good enough care of my body?

Related dreams: Belly · Paunch · Entrails · Intestines · Bleeding

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of Abhorring Someone
─────────────────────────────

In one sentence
Dreaming of loathing someone speaks of justified suspicion, but also of
selfishness creeping in.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You loathe someone: a strange dislike, and your suspicions about their
  honesty prove right
• Others loathe you: your good intentions may sour into selfishness
• Your partner loathes you: you may fall for someone who is not right for you

Depending on how you felt
• Anger or disgust: the dream may reflect a mistrust you have not voiced
• Fear of rejection: it may express worry about not being loved

Questions to ask yourself
• Is my instinct telling me to be wary of someone?
• Am I afraid I have let others down?

Related dreams: Hate · Hatred · Contempt · Enemy · Envy

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of Being Abject
────────────────────────

In one sentence
Seeing yourself wretched in a dream points to bad news and friction among
friends.

Tone: ●●○○○ negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are abject: gloomy news slows your climb toward success
• Others are abject: bickering and double-dealing among your friends

Depending on how you felt
• Discouragement: the dream often reflects weariness with your efforts
• Shame: it may express a fear of being judged or looked down on

Questions to ask yourself
• What is making me doubt myself right now?
• Are there tensions among my friends that I am avoiding?

Related dreams: Misery · Melancholy · Despair · Disgrace · Poverty

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of Your Abode
──────────────────────

In one sentence
Your dwelling in a dream concerns trust and stability: losing it means losing
your footing.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You cannot find your home: you lose faith in other people's honesty
• You have no home: setbacks in business and losses through speculation
• You change homes: urgent news and hurried journeys
• You leave your home: slander is being spread about you

Depending on how you felt
• Insecurity: the dream may reflect a lack of grounding or stability
• Restlessness: it may express a wish, or a fear, of big change

Questions to ask yourself
• Where do I truly feel at home?
• What is shaking my trust right now?

Related dreams: Home · House · Moving · Journey · Slander

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)

───────────────────────

This dream warns against a risky undertaking or neglecting your

Tone: ●●○○○ negative

Depending on what happens in the dream

Depending on how you felt

Questions to ask yourself

Dreaming of Something Hanging Above You
───────────────────────────────────────

In one sentence
Something hanging over your head is about threat or improvement, depending on
whether it holds or falls.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed: danger or progress depending on the scene

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Something hangs above you, about to fall: danger
• It falls on you: ruin or sudden disappointment
• It falls near you but misses: a narrow escape from losing money
• It is firmly fixed: your situation improves after a threatened loss

Depending on how you felt
• Apprehension: the dream often reflects a worry hanging over you
• Hope: it may express a sense that things can hold firm

Questions to ask yourself
• What threat do I feel hanging over me?
• Is what worries me really as fragile as I think?

Related dreams: Fall · Danger · Roof · Escape · Beam

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)


Dreaming of Being Abroad
────────────────────────

In one sentence
Being abroad in a dream points to a pleasant trip and a stay in another
climate.

Tone: ●●●●○ positive

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are abroad or about to go: a pleasant trip with others, and a stay away
  from home in a different climate

Depending on how you felt
• Excitement: the dream may reflect a craving for novelty and new horizons
• A need to escape: it may express a wish for a break from daily life

Questions to ask yourself
• What would I like to step away from for a while?
• What new horizon is calling me?

Related dreams: Journey · Traveling · Voyage · Tourist · Exile

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of Absalom
───────────────────

In one sentence
Absalom, the rebellious son, signals painful events and warns against hurting
those you love.

Tone: ●●○○○ negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You dream of Absalom: distressing incidents, and the risk of deeply hurting
  someone dear to you
• This or any other rebellious figure: a warning against your worse impulses
• If you are a parent: keep a careful eye on your children

Depending on how you felt
• Inner conflict: the dream may reflect a tug between loyalty and independence
• Parental worry: it may express a fear of a child drifting away

Questions to ask yourself
• Is there someone I might hurt without meaning to?
• Where am I torn between obeying and rebelling?

Related dreams: David · Son · Father · Bible · Disgrace

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of an Abscess
──────────────────────

In one sentence
An abscess in a dream mixes misfortune with compassion, but can also mean
healing after illness.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• A chronic abscess: your own troubles overwhelm you, while you feel deeply
  for others' sorrows
• An abscess or running sore: good luck and good health, after a spell of
  illness

Depending on how you felt
• Discomfort or irritation: the dream may reflect a problem that is festering
• Relief: it may express a need to lance the boil and feel better

Questions to ask yourself
• What problem am I letting fester?
• What needs to come out so I can heal?

Related dreams: Boils · Sores · Ulcer · Sickness · Festering Sore

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)


Dreaming of Absence
───────────────────

In one sentence
Dreaming of absent people often foretells their return, stronger friendships
and success.

Tone: ●●●●○ mostly positive, with one shadow

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You grieve someone's absence: sincere regret wins you lifelong friendships
• You are glad friends are absent: you will soon be rid of an enemy
• You dream of absent people: they will soon return, and your business does
  well
• Absent friends: news of them, good or bad
• They seem to stand by your bed: a worrying sign for them

Depending on how you felt
• Longing: the dream often reflects the place a faraway person holds in your
  life
• Nostalgia: it may express a wish to reconnect

Questions to ask yourself
• Who am I missing right now?
• Is there someone I should get in touch with?

Related dreams: Friend · Farewell · Parting · Visit · News

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862); A. H. Noe, The Witches' Dream Book (1885)


Dreaming of Absinthe
────────────────────

In one sentence
Absinthe in a dream points to carefree pleasures that squander your energy and
money.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are under absinthe's influence: a merry, foolish life that wastes your
  inheritance
• You drink it with your partner: beware of being swept along too fast
• You are drunk on it: you give in without resistance
• In general: you may waste your energy on pleasure

Depending on how you felt
• Euphoria: the dream may reflect a wish to let go
• Unease: it may express a fear of losing control

Questions to ask yourself
• Where am I spending too much energy on easy pleasures?
• Do I need to let go, or to pull myself together?

Related dreams: Drunkenness · Liquor · Intoxication · Wine · Lover

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of Abundance
─────────────────────

In one sentence
Abundance in a dream promises financial independence, but warns of scarcity
and strain at home.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You have plenty: fortune is kind, but your home life may suffer from your
  infidelity
• You have too much of something: the dream works by contraries and points to
  a shortage of something important to you

Depending on how you felt
• Contentment: the dream may reflect a sense of security
• Fear of want: it may express worry that it will not last

Questions to ask yourself
• What do I really need to feel fulfilled?
• Am I neglecting the people close to me for the sake of success?

Related dreams: Wealth · Plenty · Rich · Scarcity · Luxury

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)


Dreaming of Abuse
─────────────────

In one sentence
Abuse in a dream points to disputes, jealousy and losses through stubbornness.

Tone: ●●○○○ negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You abuse someone: setbacks, and money lost through overbearing persistence
• You are abused or insulted: enemies harass you, and a dispute breaks out
  with someone you do business with
• You are in love and are insulted: someone has tried to turn your sweetheart
  against you, and largely succeeded
• You hear abusive language: you draw jealousy and envy
• You use it yourself: unexpected rebuffs and remorse

Depending on how you felt
• Hurt: the dream may reflect a recent humiliation
• Pent-up anger: it may express words you are holding back

Questions to ask yourself
• Who or what is hurting me right now?
• Are there words I regret saying?

Related dreams: Insult · Quarrel · Dispute · Slander · Jealousy

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller

Dreaming of an Abyss
────────────────────

In one sentence
An abyss in a dream points to threats to your property and quarrels, unless
you manage to avoid it.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative, with a way out

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You look into an abyss: threats of seizure and personal quarrels
• You fall in: complete disappointment
• You cross it or avoid it: you regain your footing
• An abyss or deep hole: avoid travel for forty-eight hours

Depending on how you felt
• Vertigo: the dream often reflects fear of the unknown or of failure
• Helplessness: it may express a sense of standing at the edge of something
  bottomless

Questions to ask yourself
• What void do I feel I am standing in front of?
• What would help me step back from the edge?

Related dreams: Precipice · Pit · Fall · Cave · Danger

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)


Dreaming of an Academy
──────────────────────

In one sentence
An academy in a dream speaks of missed chances and knowledge poorly put to
use.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You visit an academy: you regret chances let slip through idleness
• You own one or live in one: ambitions easily defeated, and knowledge you
  struggle to apply
• You go back after finishing there: demands will be made that you cannot meet

Depending on how you felt
• Regret: the dream may reflect a feeling of not having seized your chance
• Insecurity: it may express a fear of not measuring up

Questions to ask yourself
• What opportunity have I let slip?
• Am I really putting what I learn into practice?

Related dreams: School · College · Learning · Education · High School

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of Being Accepted
──────────────────────────

In one sentence
Being accepted in a dream promises success in business or love, unless the
dream comes from anxiety.

Tone: ●●●●○ positive, with one caveat

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Your proposal is accepted: you close a deal that looked doomed
• Your sweetheart accepts you: a happy marriage
• If the dream comes from great anxiety: the opposite may follow

Depending on how you felt
• Joy: the dream may reflect a need for recognition being met
• Apprehension: it may express anxious waiting for an answer

Questions to ask yourself
• What "yes" am I waiting for right now?
• Do I accept myself?

Related dreams: Engagement · Success · Courtship · Marriage · Offer

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of an Accident
───────────────────────

In one sentence
An accident in a dream calls for caution when travelling, but can also mean an
unexpected visitor.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You dream of an accident: avoid travel for a while, as danger threatens
• An accident befalls livestock: you strive for a goal, then a friend loses as
  much helping you
• An accident happens to you or your household: you will see someone you did
  not expect

Depending on how you felt
• Anxiety: the dream often reflects a sense of losing control
• Caution: it may express a need to slow down

Questions to ask yourself
• Where am I going too fast right now?
• What am I afraid of losing control of?

Related dreams: Collision · Disaster · Danger · Traveling · Injury

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a

Dreaming of an Accordion
────────────────────────

In one sentence
An accordion in a dream brings cheer that lightens your burdens.

Tone: ●●●●○ mostly positive, with one shadow

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You hear an accordion: amusements lift you out of sadness and help you carry

• You play one: a sad event brings you closer to your sweetheart, for lasting
  happiness
• The accordion is out of tune: illness or trouble for your partner saddens

Depending on how you felt
• Comfort: the dream may reflect a need for lightness
• Melancholy: it may express a bittersweet nostalgia

Questions to ask yourself
• What helps me carry my worries more cheerfully?
• Do I need more music and fun in my life?

Dreaming of Accounts
────────────────────

In one sentence
Accounts in a dream speak of debts, disputes and sometimes a stroke of luck.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Bills are presented to you: a risky position, perhaps a legal remedy
• You pay them: a compromise in a serious dispute
• You hold accounts against others: annoyances in your business
• You balance accounts: a good sign; trouble at work and in love, then the
  respect of those around you
• You find an error in your accounts: a piece of luck
• Ink-blotted accounts: a risk of illness

Depending on how you felt
• Worry: the dream may reflect money concerns or things you must answer for
• A need for order: it may express a wish to take stock

Questions to ask yourself
• Do I have scores to settle, in money or with someone?
• What do I owe myself?

Related dreams: Debt · Ledger · Counting · Money · Addition

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)

────────────────────

In one sentence
Accusing or being accused in a dream speaks of quarrels and gossip, but can

Questions to ask yourself

Dreaming of Aches
─────────────────

In one sentence
Aches in a dream often point to lost momentum, or simply to a physical cause.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You ache: you are hesitating in business and someone else profits from your
  ideas
• You have heartache: your partner is slow to commit
• Backache: illness through carelessness
• Headache: worry over a risk taken against a rival
• In general: this dream often comes from the body and means little

Depending on how you felt
• Tiredness: the dream may reflect real exhaustion
• Frustration: it may express a sense of moving too slowly

Questions to ask yourself
• Is my body trying to tell me something?

Dreaming of Acorns
──────────────────

In one sentence
Acorns in a dream promise strength, gain and success after effort, unless they
are spoiled.

Tone: ●●●●○ mostly positive

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see acorns: pleasant things ahead and good gains
• You pick them up: success after long effort, or even a fortune from a
  wealthy relative
• You eat them: you move from a life of toil to one of ease
• You shake them from the tree: your wishes come true quickly, in business or
  love
• Green acorns, or acorns scattered on the ground: your affairs take a turn
  for the better
• Rotten acorns: disappointments and reverses
• You pull them green from the tree: haste harms your interests
• Pigs eating acorns: business setbacks unless you are careful

Depending on how you felt
• Confidence: the dream may reflect the patience of someone planting seeds
• Impatience: it may express a wish to harvest too soon

Questions to ask yourself
• What small seed am I growing right now?
• Do I have the patience to let my plans ripen?

Related dreams: Oak · Nuts · Tree · Swine · Inheritance

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862); A. H. Noe, The Witches' Dream Book (1885)


Dreaming of an Acquaintance
───────────────────────────

In one sentence
Meeting an acquaintance in a dream mirrors the state of your relationships:
calm or stormy.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You chat pleasantly with an acquaintance: business runs smoothly and there
  is little discord at home
• You argue with them: humiliations, family rifts and losses
• You are ashamed to meet them: some misconduct of yours will come out
• You have a wide circle: great interests and a love worth winning
• Your circle is small: little social success
• After this dream: you may hear from the person

Depending on how you felt
• Curiosity: the dream may reflect interest in a bond that is still shallow
• Awkwardness: it may express unease in a relationship

Questions to ask yourself
• Is there a relationship I would like to deepen?
• With whom do I have an unspoken unease?

Related dreams: Friend · Quarrel · Visit · Companion · Stranger

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862); A. H. Noe, The Witches' Dream Book (1885)

Dreaming of an Acrobat
──────────────────────

In one sentence
An acrobat in a dream speaks of risk, mockery and a reputation under attack.

Tone: ●●○○○ negative

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see acrobats: others' foolish fears keep you from risky schemes
• You perform acrobatics: you will have to answer for a stir, and enemies will
  mock you
• You see women acrobats: your name is slandered and your business hindered
• Acrobats in tights: you are seeking to please others

Depending on how you felt
• Imbalance: the dream may reflect juggling too many things

prosperity and love for others.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed, between dullness and happiness

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Seeing bananas: you may end up tied to a partner who bores you and whom you
  don't love
• Eating a banana: one reading sees a tiresome business venture and self-
  imposed duties; another sees wealth and happiness
• Rotting bananas: you'll soon get drawn into an unpleasant undertaking
• Trading in bananas: interests pile up around you without paying off
• Bananas growing on the tree: success in love
• Being handed a ripe banana by your sweetheart: a wedding is near

Depending on how you felt
• Boredom or distaste: the dream may point to a routine or relationship that
  weighs on you
• Pleasure or appetite: you may be longing for more sweetness and plenty

Questions to ask yourself
• Is there a duty I've taken on that I don't really want?
• Does what sustains me right now actually appeal to me?

Related dreams: Fruit · Figs · Dates (Fruit) · Pineapple · Marriage

Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller

─────────────────────

In one sentence

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

  you're single, a marriage soon

Depending on how you felt
• A need for warmth: the dream often mirrors a wish for a comforting home
• Overflow: it may reflect emotions looking for a way out

• Which feeling needs a way out?

• Others go through a doorway: your efforts to get your affairs back on track
  will fail
• A door you close falls off its hinges and hurts someone: careless advice
  from you will harm a friend
• A door falls when someone else tries to lock it: you'll learn of a friend's
  misfortune and be unable to help

Depending on how you felt
• A threshold: the dream often reflects a transition or an opportunity
• Nostalgia or fear: perhaps a longing for a safe place, or a fear of being
  turned away

Questions to ask yourself
• Which door am I hesitating to open?
• Where do I truly feel at home?

Related dreams: Doorbell · Door Knocker · Key · Lock · House

Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller

Your father in a dream signals a difficulty where wise advice will be needed,
though seeing him can also be lucky.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see your father: a difficulty you will get through with good counsel, or
  simply good luck
• Your father appears as dead: your business is struggling, so be careful
• Your late father appears and you are in a relationship: your partner may be
  unfaithful
• You see your father die: illness

Depending on how you felt
• Nostalgia or a need for support: the dream may reflect a search for guidance
• Worry: it may reveal concern for a parent or a complicated bond

Questions to ask yourself
• What advice do I need right now?
• What did my father pass on to me, and what am I doing with it?

Related dreams: Mother · Family · Parents · Father-in-Law · Advice

────────────────

In one sentence
Fire is a good sign as long as it doesn't burn you: it brings prosperity,
success and love, but also flashes of anger.

Tone: ●●●●○ mostly positive, unless you are burned

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see a fire and are not burned: lasting prosperity
• Your own home or business is burning: a loving household and booming
  business
• Someone else's house is on fire: a sad event, such as a friend's misfortune
• You fight a fire without being burned: plenty of work and worry
• You see the ruins after a fire: bad luck, but unexpected good fortune will
  lift you again
• You light a fire: pleasant surprises and visits to distant friends
• A huge blaze: success, honours and a safe voyage
• You are burned, or fire falls from the sky: serious danger and enemies who
  will harm you
• You play with fire: a quarrel at home; a burning house can also mean anger

Depending on how you felt
• Passion: the dream may reflect intense energy or desire
• Anger: it may reveal a feeling that is smouldering

Questions to ask yourself
• What am I passionate about right now?
• Is there anger I'm letting smoulder?

Related dreams: Burning · Conflagration · Flame · Burns · Smoke

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862); A. H. Noe, The Witches' Dream Book (1885); Anonymous, The
Interpretation of Dreams and Moles (1805)

Flying is often an excellent omen of rising fortune and happiness, but it
depends how high you go, what lies below and whether you fall.

Tone: ●●●●○ mostly positive, depending on the flight

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are flying: a rise in fortune, lasting happiness and a faithful partner
• You fly through the air: a quick journey or sudden news
• You fly very high: trouble in your marriage or relationship
• You fly close to the ground: illness or unease you will recover from
• You fly over muddy water or broken ground: bad luck; guard your private
  affairs
• You fly over green trees or see the sun: prosperity despite your fears
• You fly on black wings, or out past the planets: bitter disappointment and
  troubles
• You fall while flying: a downfall; if you wake as you fall, you will recover
• You try to fly and cannot: some restraint will hold you back from your goal

Depending on how you felt
• Freedom: the dream often reflects drive and a wish to rise
• Anxiety: a difficult flight may show a fear of losing your footing

Questions to ask yourself
• What would I like to break free from?
• What keeps me from taking off?

Related dreams: Wings · Flying Machine · Air · Fall · Journey

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862); A. H. Noe, The Witches' Dream Book (1885); Anonymous, The
Interpretation of Dreams and Moles (1805)

Hay is a dream of prosperity, influence and success.

Tone: ●●●●● very positive, unless you sell it

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You mow hay: much good in life, abundant crops and influence
• Fields of freshly cut hay: unusual prosperity
• You haul hay into the barn: assured fortune and a big profit
• You rake hay together: you'll lead assemblies
• Loads of hay passing in the street: influential strangers who add to your
  enjoyment
• You feed hay to livestock: you'll help someone who repays you with affection
  and advancement
• You sell hay: losses and accidents, the one bad sign

Depending on how you felt
• Contentment: the dream often reflects satisfaction in work well done
• Foresight: you may be thinking of setting something aside

Questions to ask yourself
• What am I storing up for later?
• Which piece of work deserves credit?

Related dreams: Raking · Harvest · Barn · Straw · Meadow

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862); A. H. Noe, The Witches' Dream Book (1885)

Dreaming of a Horse
───────────────────

In one sentence
A horse is an excellent sign of prosperity and advancement, especially if you
ride it easily; a wounded, dead or bucking horse points to setbacks.

Tone: ●●●●○ mostly positive

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You ride a spirited horse easily: your fortunes rise, and a happy marriage
  is in sight
• A white horse: prosperity and good company; if soiled and lean, a jealous
  friend will betray your trust
• A black or dark horse: success, but with delays, discontent or a temptation
  to deceive
• A runaway horse: a friend's or employer's folly harms your interests, or
  unexpected, unwelcome business
• A horse bucks or throws you: a strong rival and hard-won desires; a kick:
  rejection by someone you love
• You catch and harness a horse: a marked improvement in business; if you fail
  to catch it, fortune will let you down
• You ford a clear stream on horseback: good fortune and rich pleasures; if
  the water is murky, joys that fall a little short
• A wounded or dead horse: troubles among friends, or business stalling
• You buy a horse: a gain; you sell or swap one: a loss, or someone will cheat
  you
• You ride up a hill and reach the top: a remarkable and lasting rise; riding
  downhill, disappointment

Depending on how you felt
• Drive: the dream often reflects your vitality and wish to move forward
• A question of control: you may be asking whether you hold the reins of your
  life

Questions to ask yourself
• Am I holding the reins, or being carried away?
• What am I galloping towards right now?

Related dreams: Mare · Stallion · Riding · Foal · Horseshoe

In one sentence
Macaroni foretells small losses, but also savings and sometimes the arrival of
a stranger.

Tone: ●●●○○ neutral

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Eating macaroni: small losses
• Macaroni in large quantities: strict economy will save you money
• If you are single: a stranger will come into your life

Depending on how you felt
• A need for comfort: the dream may reflect a wish for simplicity
• Caution: it may express concern about money

Questions to ask yourself
• Where could I be more careful with spending?
• Am I open to meeting someone new?

Related dreams: Noodles · Eating · Meals · Stranger · Flour

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)

Dreaming of Being Mad
─────────────────────

In one sentence
Being mad in a dream, or among mad people, reads in reverse: long life, wealth
and success.

Tone: ●●●●○ positive (by contrast)

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You are mad, or among mad people: long life, riches, a happy marriage and
  success
• If you are in a lawsuit: it will go strongly in your favor
• If you farm: an accident with livestock, but plentiful crops

Depending on how you felt
• Fear of losing your grip: the dream may reflect a time of great strain
• Freedom: it may express a wish to break with convention

Questions to ask yourself

Dreaming of Marriage
────────────────────

In one sentence
Marriage is a split omen: attending a joyful wedding can mean pleasure and
success, but marrying yourself often foretells trials and sorrow.

Tone: ●●○○○ mostly negative, with some happy readings

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Attending a wedding where guests are cheerful and colorful: great enjoyment
  and good news
• Guests in black or somber colors: mourning and sorrow
• Being an attendant or guest at a wedding: kindness from loved ones and
  promising business
• Getting married yourself: unpleasant news from someone absent, or an omen of
  hardship or poverty
• Marrying a very old, frail person: much trouble and illness
• A former love passes during the ceremony, looking reproachful: a friend's
  coldness will drive you to despair
• A mishap at the wedding: distress or illness in the family
• Being an unhappy or indifferent bride or groom: disappointment in love;
  beware of enemies

Depending on how you felt
• Commitment: the dream often reflects thoughts about a bond or union, not
  necessarily romantic

───────────────────────

In one sentence
A handsome, healthy nephew promises a welcome income; otherwise,
disappointment and discomfort.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Your nephew looks handsome and well: a pleasing competence is coming your
  way
• He looks unwell: disappointment and discomfort

Depending on how you felt
• Passing things on: the dream often reflects what you hope to hand down
• Concern for family: it may show your attention to the next generation

Questions to ask yourself
• What would I like to pass on?
• How are the younger members of my family doing?

Related dreams: Niece · Uncle · Aunt · Relatives · Family

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)


Dreaming of a Nest
──────────────────

In one sentence
A nest promises a thriving venture and a happy home, unless it is empty or
full of bad eggs.

Tone: ●●●●○ fairly positive

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see birds' nests: a prosperous venture
• If you are young: a change of home
• A hen's nest: you will be drawn to home life, and children will be cheerful
• An empty nest: sorrow at a friend's absence
• A nest full of broken or bad eggs: disappointment and failure

Depending on how you felt
• A need for home: the dream often reflects a wish for a safe, warm place
• Fear of emptiness: it may show a worry that people are drifting away

Questions to ask yourself
• Where is my nest right now?
• Who is missing from my home?

Related dreams: Bird's Nest · Birds · Egg · Hen · Home

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901)

A piano promises joy if the music is sweet and frustration if it's discordant.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• You see a piano: a joyful occasion
• Sweet, rich music: success and health; lively tunes, thrift and happiness at
  home
• Discordant music: many exasperating matters to deal with
• Sad, plaintive music: sorrowful news
• A broken or out-of-tune piano: dissatisfaction with yourself and
  disappointment at loved ones' failures
• An old-fashioned piano: you've ignored past advice and opportunities; don't
  do it again
• You play difficult, enchanting music: you'll win over someone who has been
  indifferent
• You buy or are given a piano: money trouble

Depending on how you felt
• Harmony or dissonance: the dream may reflect how in tune your relationships
  feel
• A need for expression: a wish to put your feelings into something

Questions to ask yourself
• What rings true, and what sounds off, in my life right now?
• Which feeling do I want to express?

Related dreams: Music · Musical Instruments · Concert · Organ · Musician

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)

Dreaming of Teeth
─────────────────

In one sentence
Teeth are among the darkest dreams in the tradition: illness, loss and
bereavement, with a few bright exceptions.

Tone: ●○○○○ very negative, with a few happy exceptions

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Loose or falling teeth: setbacks, bad news, losing friends or loved ones
• The more fall out, the worse it is: one means bad news; all of them, real
  hardship
• Decayed or broken teeth: strain on your health or business
• A dentist pulls a tooth: a long illness
• A tooth is filled: you'll recover something you lost
• You brush your teeth: you'll have to fight to keep your position
• Tartar falls away leaving sound teeth: a passing ailment that leaves you
  wiser
• You admire your white teeth: pleasant work and wishes fulfilled
• A new tooth comes in: the birth of a child with a bright future

Depending on how you felt
• Anxiety: this very common dream often mirrors a fear of losing control or
  looking bad
• Vulnerability: worry about your health, your image or the people you love

Questions to ask yourself
• Where do I feel I'm losing my grip?
• Am I worried about how I come across?

Related dreams: Toothache · Toothless · Dentist · Mouth · Jaws

Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller

Interpretation of Dreams and Moles (1805)

depending on what happens to it.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Seeing a watch: well-judged investments will make you prosperous
• Checking the time: rivals will undercut your efforts
• Breaking it: distress and loss; dropping its crystal: carelessness or bad
  company
• Losing it: trouble at home, though by another reading losing a gold watch
  means business success
• Stealing one: an enemy will attack your reputation
• Giving one as a gift: you will neglect your interests for unworthy pastimes
• Buying a gold one: hard times; being given one: luck and money

Depending on how you felt
• Time pressure: the dream often reflects a feeling that the hours are
  slipping by
• A need for control: you may be afraid of missing the right moment

Questions to ask yourself
• Do I feel short of time?
• What am I waiting for the 'right moment' to do?

Related dreams: Clock · Gold · Jewellery · Chain

Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller

─────────────────

In one sentence
Clear water promises prosperity and pleasure; muddy or troubled water warns of
danger, illness and grief.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed, depending on the water

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Seeing or being on clear water: prosperity and joy
• Muddy or rough water: danger and gloom
• Water rising in your house: you will struggle against bad influences, and
  give in unless it goes down
• Bailing it out while your feet get wet: trouble and illness, which vigilance
  will help you head off
• Falling into muddy water: bitter mistakes and deep grief
• Drinking clear, fresh water: your hopes come true; drinking muddy water:
  illness
• Playing with water or being sprayed: a sudden awakening to love, which will
  be returned
• A wide stretch of water you can't get across: you're starting something
  without the means to succeed

Depending on how you felt
• Overflowing feelings: water often mirrors the state of your inner world
• A need for clarity: you may be trying to see a situation more clearly

Questions to ask yourself
• Are my emotions calm or churned up right now?
• What am I trying to cross without the means to do it?

• Your family objects: your engagement will upset your relatives
• Your partner marries someone else: needless fears, as they will keep their
  promises

• Marrying someone handsome: joy; someone unattractive: discontent

Depending on how you felt
• Excitement or nerves: the dream often reflects an approaching commitment or
  big change
• Worry: you may be wondering what you're leaving behind

• What is changing in my life right now?

• Wheat in sacks or barrels: success is close and your love life on firm
  ground
• Your granary is poorly covered and the grain gets wet: you've made money
  without securing your rights, and enemies will chip away at them
• Rubbing out a head of wheat and eating it: you will work hard and secure
  your rights
• Climbing a hill by pulling yourself up on wheat stalks: great prosperity and
  distinction
• Walking in a wheat field: wealth, a happy marriage, lawsuits won and success
  all round

Depending on how you felt
• Gratitude: the dream may reflect a sense that your efforts are bearing fruit
• A need for security: you may long for abundance and stability

Questions to ask yourself
• What have I planted that's starting to grow?
• How can I protect what I've harvested?

Related dreams: Grain · Harvest · Corn and Cornfield · Bread · Threshing

  them: worry over a spendthrift friend
• Healthy cattle yoked in harmony: a happy marriage, soon for those who are
  single
• Cattle straining against the yoke: marital trouble

Depending on how you felt
• A sense of constraint: the dream may reflect heavy obligations
• Partnership: you may be thinking about what it means to pull together

Questions to ask yourself
• Which constraint am I accepting without choosing it?
• Who am I pulling in the same direction with?

Related dreams: Oxen · Ox · Harness · Marriage · Plow

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)


Dreaming of Youth
─────────────────

In one sentence
Youth in a dream sets seeing young people, a good sign, against becoming young
again, which mostly points to regret and decline.

Tone: ●●●○○ mixed

Depending on what happens in the dream
• Seeing young people: family quarrels mended and a good time to start new
  ventures
• Dreaming of youths more generally: you'll live to a great age
• Seeing young people at school: prosperity and usefulness will surround you
• Seeing yourself young again: you'll try hard to recover lost chances and
  still fail, and for an older person the omen is grave
• Seeing your grown child as an infant again: old wounds will heal and hope
  will return
• That child seeming to be dying: misfortune and misery

Depending on how you felt
• Nostalgia: the dream often reflects longing for a past time or missed
  chances
• A wish for renewal: it may mirror a desire to recover energy and hope

Questions to ask yourself
• What do I regret not having done?
• What fresh start could I make today?

Related dreams: Age · Child · School · Old Man · Wrinkles

References: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a
Dream (1901); F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller
(1862)
